explaining a delay.title: Sorry for the Slow Reply

meeting someone new.title: At a Conference

meeting someone new.title: A Friend of a Friend

meeting someone new.title: At a Language Exchange
sentences: Hi, are you here for the language exchange as well?

planning a trip.title: Italy or Greece?
sentences: I can't decide whether to go to Italy or Greece this summer.

If I were you, I'd go to Greece and visit a few islands.

planning a trip.title: What Should I Pack?
sentences: I've never been to a cold country, so I don't know what to pack.

Should I bring my laptop, or will that just be extra weight?

planning a trip.title: A Trip on a Budget
sentences: We're trying to plan a trip without spending too much money.

If we travel by bus instead of train, we'll save quite a bit.

a job interview answer.title: My Greatest Weakness
sentences: I'd say my biggest weakness is that I find it hard to delegate.
In the past, I tried to do everything myself to make it perfect.
Recently, I've been learning to trust my team more.
I've noticed that we actually get better results that way.

a job interview answer.title: Why I Left My Last Job
sentences: I really enjoyed my last job, and I learned a great deal there.
However, after four years, I felt I had stopped growing.
I was looking for a role with more responsibility and new challenges.
When I saw this position, it seemed like the perfect next step.
I'm especially excited about the chance to lead international projects.

a job interview answer.title: Working Under Pressure
sentences: In my last role, we often had very tight deadlines.
Once, a client changed their requirements just two days before launch.
I stayed calm, organized the tasks, and kept everyone informed.
We managed to deliver on time, and the client was really pleased.

ordering coffee.title: Morning Rush Order
sentences: Hi, could I get a large latte to go, please?
Actually, can you make it with oat milk instead?
I'm running late, so I'll grab it at the end of the counter.
Oh, and could you throw in one of those blueberry muffins?
Thanks a lot, I'll tap my card right here.

ordering coffee.title: Wrong Drink Mixup
sentences: Sorry, I think this isn't the drink I ordered.
I asked for a flat white, but this looks like a cappuccino.
No worries, these things happen when it's this busy.
I'll just wait here while you make another one.
That's perfect, thanks for sorting it out so quickly.

ordering coffee.title: Trying Something New
sentences: I usually stick to black coffee, but I fancy a change today.
What would you recommend for someone who doesn't like things too sweet?
Oh, a cortado sounds good, I'll give that a try.
Could I have it in a mug, since I'm staying in?
I'll come back and let you know if I'm hooked.

a phone call with a client.title: Following Up on a Proposal
sentences: Hi Sarah, I'm just calling to follow up on our proposal.
Have you had a chance to look it over yet?
No rush at all, I just wanted to check in.
If anything's unclear, I'm happy to walk you through it.
Shall I call you back later in the week, then?

a phone call with a client.title: Rescheduling a Call
sentences: Hello, it's Mark from the design team, how are you doing?
I'm afraid something's come up and I need to move our meeting.
Would Thursday afternoon work for you instead?
Great, I'll send over a new invite right after this call.
Sorry again for the short notice, and thanks for being flexible.

a phone call with a client.title: Handling a Complaint
sentences: I completely understand why you're frustrated about the late delivery.
Let me look into it and find out what went wrong.
I'll get back to you by the end of the day.
In the meantime, we'll take care of the shipping costs.
Thanks for bearing with us while we sort this out.

small talk with a coworker.title: Monday Morning Chat
sentences: Morning! Did you manage to get some rest over the weekend?
I'm still trying to wake up, to be honest.
This coffee machine takes forever, doesn't it?
Anyway, are you going to the training session later?
I'll save you a seat if I get there first.

small talk with a coworker.title: The Office Is Freezing
sentences: Is it just me, or is it freezing in here today?
I think someone turned the air conditioning up again.
I've started bringing a jumper to work just in case.

small talk with a coworker.title: Lunch Plans
sentences: Hey, are you heading out for lunch anytime soon?
A few of us are trying out that new Thai place.
You're welcome to come along if you're not too busy.
I've heard their noodles are really worth checking out.
Cool, we'll meet by the lifts in ten minutes.

asking for directions.title: Lost Near the Station
sentences: Excuse me, could you help me out for a second?
I'm trying to find my way to the central station.
Should I keep going straight or turn around here?
Oh, so it's just past the bridge on the left?
Brilliant, thanks so much, I'd have been wandering around forever.

asking for directions.title: Looking for a Pharmacy
sentences: Sorry to bother you, is there a pharmacy around here?
I've been walking up and down this street for ages.
So I go down this road and take the second right?
And it's next to the bakery, opposite the bank?
Great, I really appreciate you pointing me in the right direction.

asking for directions.title: Finding the Hotel
sentences: Hi, I think I've got turned around somewhere.
Do you know how to get to the Riverside Hotel from here?
Is it within walking distance, or should I catch a bus?

a quick team meeting.title: Monday Check In
sentences: Okay everyone, let's keep this short and get started.
First, how are we getting on with the website update?
Great, so we're on track to wrap it up by Friday.
Does anyone need help or have something blocking them?

a quick team meeting.title: Splitting the Tasks
sentences: So we've got three main tasks to get through this week.
Anna, could you take charge of the client report?
James and I will deal with the budget figures.
If anything comes up, just give us a shout.

a quick team meeting.title: Quick Project Update
sentences: I just wanted to bring everyone up to speed quickly.
The client has pushed back the launch by a couple of weeks.
That gives us a bit more time to iron out the bugs.

talking about the weekend.title: A Relaxing Weekend
sentences: How was your weekend, did you get up to anything fun?

I finally caught up on that series everyone's talking about.

talking about the weekend.title: A Busy Family Weekend
sentences: Honestly, I feel like I need another weekend to recover.

talking about the weekend.title: Weekend Plans Fell Through
sentences: I was supposed to go camping, but the plans fell through.

at the doctor.title: A Persistent Cough
sentences: I've had this cough for about two weeks now.

at the doctor.title: Twisted Ankle
sentences: I think I twisted my ankle while I was out running.

at the doctor.title: Picking Up a Prescription
sentences: Hi, I'm here to pick up a repeat prescription.

returning something at a store.title: Shoes That Don't Fit

sentences: Excuse me, these headphones stopped working after just two days.

returning something at a store.title: Unwanted Gift

explaining a delay.title: Stuck in Traffic
sentences: Hi, I'm really sorry, but I'm running a bit late.

meeting someone new.title: At a Friend's Party
sentences: Hi, I don't think we've met, I'm Daniel.

sentences: I can't quite put my finger on it, but something feels off.

I should've flagged it sooner instead of hoping I'd catch up.

sentences: I get the sense there's a bit more to this than you're letting on.
If there's been a shift in priorities on your side, do say.
We'd much rather adapt now than find ourselves out of step later.
Nothing you tell me will put our relationship in jeopardy, I promise.
Right, that puts things in a rather different light, thank you.

a phone call with a client.title: Declining Extra Work
sentences: I'm genuinely flattered you thought of us for this.
But in all honesty, it's somewhat outside our wheelhouse.
I'd hate to take it on and deliver something half baked.
I could put you in touch with someone who does this brilliantly.
And naturally, the core work remains our top priority throughout.

small talk with a coworker.title: Dry Humour About Meetings
sentences: Another meeting that could quite easily have been an email, then.
I lost the will to live somewhere around the third slide.
Still, I did learn that synergy is apparently making a comeback.
I'm half tempted to start a bingo card for next week.
Don't look at me like that, you know you'd play.

small talk with a coworker.title: Tactful Gossip
sentences: I'm not one to gossip, but have you heard about Mike?
Apparently he's handed in his notice, rather out of the blue.
I gather things hadn't been entirely rosy with his manager for a while.
Mind you, that's purely hearsay, so take it with a pinch of salt.
Either way, the place won't quite be the same without him.

small talk with a coworker.title: Weather Grumbling
sentences: Glorious weather we're having, if you happen to be a duck.
I made the fatal error of trusting the forecast this morning.
My umbrella turned inside out before I'd even reached the bus stop.
I've resigned myself to being vaguely damp until about lunchtime.
Roll on summer, though I daresay we'll complain about the heat.

asking for directions.title: Overly Polite Tourist
sentences: I'm terribly sorry to accost you, but I'm hopelessly lost.
I'm after a little bookshop that's meant to be tucked away round here.
My phone's insisting it's right where we're standing, which seems unlikely.
Ah, down that alley, I'd have walked straight past it.
You've been immensely kind, I won't keep you any longer.

asking for directions.title: A Local Knows Best
sentences: Is there a quicker way to the station than the high street?
I'd steer clear of the high street, it's absolute gridlock at this hour.
Your best bet is to cut through the back of the market.
Bear left at the old church, then just follow your nose.
You'll know you've overshot it if you end up at the canal.

asking for directions.title: Misleading Satnav
sentences: I'm beginning to suspect my satnav has a rather cruel sense of humour.
It's sent me down the same dead end three times now.
Is there a road that actually connects to the old mill?
Ah, so it's only accessible from the far side of the village.
That would explain a great deal, thank you, I'm much obliged.

a quick team meeting.title: Navigating Competing Priorities
sentences: I'm conscious we're all stretched, so I'll keep this tight.
We've got two equally urgent requests and frankly not enough hands.
Rather than spread ourselves too thin, I'd suggest we sequence them.
I'll take the flak from whichever stakeholder ends up waiting.
Does anyone see a glaring flaw in that before we commit?

a quick team meeting.title: Diplomatic Pushback
sentences: I take your point, but I'm not entirely convinced it's that straightforward.
My worry is that we're solving the symptom rather than the cause.
If we patch it now, we're simply storing up problems for later.
I'd be inclined to take the hit and fix it properly.
But I'm happy to be talked round if the numbers say otherwise.

a quick team meeting.title: Ending on Time
sentences: Right, I'm acutely aware we're bumping up against the hour.
Let's not reopen the debate on branding, we've been round the houses.
Can we agree to take that offline with the relevant people?
Everyone clear on their actions, or shall I circulate a summary?
Splendid, then I'll give you back five minutes of your day.

talking about the weekend.title: Understated Brag
sentences: Oh, nothing much, just popped over to Paris for a long lunch.
I know, it sounds frightfully decadent when I say it out loud.
In my defence, the train tickets were practically being given away.
We spent most of it ambling along the river and eating far too much.
Next weekend will be a sobering return to laundry and admin.

talking about the weekend.title: A Weekend That Went Sideways
sentences: Well, it certainly didn't go according to plan, put it that way.
We'd booked a cosy cottage, only to find the heating had packed in.
Cue two nights huddled round a fire in every layer we owned.
In hindsight, it was rather charming, though it didn't feel it then.
I suspect it'll become one of those stories we dine out on.

talking about the weekend.title: Deliberate Idleness
sentences: I made a conscious decision to do absolutely nothing, and it was bliss.
Phone off, no plans, nobody expecting anything of me whatsoever.
I read a novel cover to cover, which I haven't done in years.
There's something quietly radical about refusing to be productive.
I'd thoroughly recommend it, though it's harder than it sounds.

at the doctor.title: Downplaying Symptoms
sentences: I'm probably wasting your time, but my wife insisted I come in.
There's this nagging pain in my chest that comes and goes.
It's not excruciating, more a sort of dull, persistent ache.
I'd put it down to stress, but it's been dragging on for weeks.
Fine, I'll concede it's better to err on the side of caution.

at the doctor.title: Asking the Right Questions
sentences: Before we go down that route, could I ask a few questions?
What would the realistic downsides of the procedure actually be?
And if we held off for a while, would that narrow my options?
I'm not trying to second guess you, I just like to understand things.
That's really helpful, I feel far better equipped to decide now.

at the doctor.title: Admitting Feeling Low
sentences: I've been feeling rather flat lately, and I can't seem to shake it.
Nothing dramatic has happened, which almost makes it harder to explain.
I'm still functioning, but everything seems to take enormous effort.
I'm reluctant to make a fuss, but my sister thought I should come.
It's a relief, frankly, just to have said it out loud.

returning something at a store.title: Firm but Courteous
sentences: I appreciate you're only following policy, and I don't hold it against you.
But the fault was clearly there from the outset, not caused by me.
Consumer law is fairly unambiguous on that point, as I understand it.
I'd rather resolve this amicably here than escalate it unnecessarily.
Thank you, I knew we'd find a sensible way through it.

returning something at a store.title: Sheepish Return
sentences: This is mildly embarrassing, but I bought entirely the wrong size.
I was so convinced I knew my measurements that I didn't try it on.
Pride comes before a fall, as they say.
Would you be kind enough to swap it for the next size up?
You're a star, I'll check the fit before leaving next time.

returning something at a store.title: Return Without Packaging
sentences: I'm afraid I've rather foolishly thrown away the original packaging.
The item itself is untouched, it simply turned out to be surplus to requirements.
I quite understand if that complicates matters on your end.
Would a credit note be a workable compromise in that case?
That's eminently reasonable, thank you for being so accommodating.

explaining a delay.title: Candid Update to the Boss
sentences: I'll spare you the excuses and give it to you straight.
We're running about a week behind, and it's largely self inflicted.
We were too optimistic at the outset and didn't build in any slack.
I've reworked the plan, and I'm confident the new date will hold.
Lesson learned, I'll be rather more conservative with estimates from now on.

explaining a delay.title: Apologising to a Friend
sentences: I've been appallingly slow getting back to you, and I'm sorry.
It's been one of those months where everything piles up at once.
That's not an excuse, mind, just a bit of context.
Your message genuinely meant a lot, even if I was hopeless at replying.
Let me make amends, dinner's on me whenever you're free.

explaining a delay.title: Delayed Departure Announcement
sentences: We do apologise for the delay to this evening's departure.
An earlier technical issue has had a knock on effect across the schedule.
The crew are doing everything they can to get us underway promptly.
We'll update you the moment we have a firmer departure time.
In the meantime, thank you for your continued patience and understanding.

meeting someone new.title: Dinner Party Introduction
sentences: I don't believe we've been introduced, I'm Clara, the host's sister.
So how do you know Paul, through work or something more scandalous?
Ah, the infamous book club, I've heard all the stories.
I must say, you're not quite what I'd pictured from his descriptions.
That's a compliment, I promise, he does rather exaggerate.

meeting someone new.title: Meeting a Partner's Parents
sentences: It's lovely to finally put a face to the name.
Emma talks about you both constantly, all of it glowing, I assure you.
I brought a bottle of red, though I gather you're the real connoisseur.
Do forgive me if I'm a touch nervous, it's quite the occasion.
Something smells divine, I hope you haven't gone to too much trouble.

meeting someone new.title: Unexpected Connection
sentences: Sorry, did you say you grew up in Galway as well?
How extraordinary, we must have been at school around the same time.
Don't tell me you knew the Murphys from down by the harbour.
Honestly, the world gets smaller every single day, doesn't it?
We'll have to compare notes properly over a drink sometime.

planning a trip.title: Reconciling Different Tastes
sentences: The trick is finding somewhere that caters to both our whims.
You want mountains and solitude, I want museums and decent wine.
Northern Italy might just be the sweet spot, if you think about it.
We could split our time between the lakes and a couple of cities.
Neither of us gets everything, but nobody ends up sulking either.

planning a trip.title: Talking Down an Overplanner
sentences: I admire your thoroughness, truly, but this itinerary is borderline military.
There's no breathing room for anything serendipitous to happen.
Some of my fondest travel memories were complete accidents, you know.
How about we keep the essentials and leave the afternoons open?
Trust me, the city will reward us for loosening our grip.

planning a trip.title: A Long Overdue Pilgrimage
sentences: I've been meaning to walk the Camino for the best part of a decade.
Every year something conveniently crops up and I quietly shelve it.
This time I've booked the flights, so there's no wriggling out.
I'm under no illusions, my knees will have plenty to say about it.
But I suspect it's precisely the sort of reset I need.

a job interview answer.title: Addressing a Career Gap
sentences: You'll notice there's a gap on my CV, and I'm happy to address it.
I took a year out to care for a family member who was unwell.
It was challenging, but it sharpened my priorities and my patience considerably.
I kept my skills current through freelance projects and a few courses.
I'd say I've come back with more clarity than I left with.

a job interview answer.title: Learning From Failure
sentences: The project that taught me most was, rather fittingly, one that failed.
We'd committed to an ambitious launch without properly testing our assumptions.
When it fell flat, my instinct was to defend the decisions we'd made.
In retrospect, the more useful move was to own it and dissect it openly.
I've since built that kind of candid post mortem into every project.

a job interview answer.title: Why Should We Hire You
sentences: I won't pretend I'm the only qualified candidate you'll see.
What I'd bring, I think, is a knack for translating between teams.
I'm equally comfortable with engineers and with the commercial side.
That tends to smooth out friction before it becomes costly.
And frankly, I'm genuinely excited by where this company is heading.
